questions.text:
Consider the following statements about sessions of the Indian National Congress.
1. The first session in 1885 at Bombay was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.
2. The Lahore session of 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted the resolution for Purna Swaraj.
3. Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Nagpur session of 1920 that approved Non-Cooperation.
questions.explanation: Gandhi presided over only one session, at Belgaum in 1924. The Nagpur session of 1920 was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.
steps: Spot what the question tests: INC sessions and presidents.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Linking Non-Cooperation with Gandhi's presidency.
So the answer is option C: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Linking Non-Cooperation with Gandhi's presidency.

questions.text:
Match List I (Battle) with List II (Outcome).
A. Wandiwash (1760)  B. Third Panipat (1761)  C. Buxar (1764)  D. Plassey (1757).
1. British victory over the French in south India  2. Afghan victory over the Marathas  3. Company victory over a coalition that included the Mughal Emperor  4. Victory helped by the defection of a Nawab's commander
questions.explanation: Wandiwash decided the Anglo-French struggle; Panipat was won by Abdali; Buxar by Hector Munro against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II; Plassey with Mir Jafar's help.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Battles of the 1750s-1760s.
Option A (A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4) is out: Wandiwash and Panipat are swapped.
Option B (A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3) is out: Buxar and Plassey are swapped.
Option D (A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4) is out: Panipat and Buxar are swapped.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing the dates of the mid-eighteenth-century battles.
So the answer is option C: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.
questions.trap: Mixing the dates of the mid-eighteenth-century battles.

questions.text: Which Delhi Sultan set up the Diwan-i-Mustakhraj to recover arrears of revenue?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji created the Diwan-i-Mustakhraj as part of his revenue reforms.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Departments of the Delhi Sultanate.
Option B (Firoz Shah Tughlaq) is out: He founded the Diwan-i-Khairat for charity.
Option C (Balban) is out: He reorganised the army department, not arrears.
Option D (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) is out: He set up the Diwan-i-Kohi for agriculture.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing a Tughlaq ruler known for another Diwan.
So the answer is option A: Alauddin Khalji.
questions.trap: Choosing a Tughlaq ruler known for another Diwan.
wrongReasons: He founded the Diwan-i-Khairat for charity
He reorganised the army department, not arrears
He set up the Diwan-i-Kohi for agriculture

questions.text: Who was the first Viceroy of India after the Government of India Act, 1858?
questions.explanation: Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India.
steps: Spot what the question tests: First and last of each office.
Option A (Lord Dalhousie) is out: He was Governor-General before the Revolt.
Option B (Lord Ripon) is out: He served in 1880-84.
Option C (Lord Curzon) is out: He served in 1899-1905.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the Governor-General of the annexation era.
So the answer is option D: Lord Canning.
questions.trap: Choosing the Governor-General of the annexation era.
questions.revise: First and last of each office
wrongReasons: He was Governor-General before the Revolt

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties.
1. They were added by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
2. The eleventh duty, relating to education of children, was added by the 86th Amendment.
3. They are enforceable by courts as the Fundamental Rights are.
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable; no court can enforce them directly.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Fundamental Duties: Article 51A.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Assuming that anything in Part IV-A is enforceable.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Assuming that anything in Part IV-A is enforceable.

questions.text: The right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years was inserted as Article 21A by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment, 2002 inserted Article 21A.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Key amendments.
Option A (42nd Amendment) is out: Added the Fundamental Duties and the Preamble words.
Option B (44th Amendment) is out: Restored rights after the Emergency.
Option D (73rd Amendment) is out: Added Panchayati Raj.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing it with the Directive Principle for early education.
So the answer is option C: 86th Amendment.
questions.trap: Confusing it with the Directive Principle for early education.
wrongReasons: Added the Fundamental Duties and the Preamble words

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Governor of a State.
1. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
2. The Governor can promulgate an ordinance while the State Legislature is in session.
3. The Governor can reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President.
questions.explanation: Under Article 213 the Governor can issue ordinances only when the Legislature is not in session.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Governor's legislative powers: Arts 200, 213.
Options A and C are out: Includes statement 2, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 2 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Ignoring the 'not in session' condition.
So the answer is option B: 1 and 3 only.
questions.trap: Ignoring the 'not in session' condition.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India.
1. It derives its authority from Article 324.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
3. It conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
questions.explanation: Local-body elections are conducted by State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Election Commission vs State Election Commission.
Options B and C are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Merging the Union and State election bodies.
So the answer is option A: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Merging the Union and State election bodies.
questions.revise: Election Commission vs State Election Commission

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT recorded in the current account of the balance of payments?
options: Receipts from services such as software exports
questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment is a capital/financial account item.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Current vs capital account.
Options A and C are out: Part of the current account.
Option B (Remittances sent by workers abroad) is out: Part of the current account (secondary income).
Common slip to avoid: Counting investment flows as current account items.
So the answer is option D: Foreign direct investment.
questions.trap: Counting investment flows as current account items.
wrongReasons: Part of the current account (secondary income)

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's policy rates.
1. The Marginal Standing Facility rate is 25 basis points below the repo rate.
2. The Standing Deposit Facility rate is the floor of the policy corridor.
3. The Bank Rate is aligned with the MSF rate.
questions.explanation: The MSF rate is 25 bps above the repo rate and forms the upper end of the corridor.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Policy corridor: SDF < repo < MSF.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 1 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Putting MSF below repo.
So the answer is option C: 2 and 3 only.
questions.trap: Putting MSF below repo.

questions.text: In which type of unemployment is the marginal productivity of some workers zero, so that their removal does not reduce output?
questions.explanation: In disguised unemployment, extra workers add nothing to output, as on small farms.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of unemployment.
Option B (Seasonal unemployment) is out: Workers are idle only in the off season.
Option C (Frictional unemployment) is out: Arises while changing jobs.
Option D (Cyclical unemployment) is out: Arises from downturns in the business cycle.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing seasonal unemployment.
So the answer is option A: Disguised unemployment.
questions.trap: Choosing seasonal unemployment.
wrongReasons: Workers are idle only in the off season
Arises from downturns in the business cycle

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Indian weather phenomena.
1. Loo is a hot, dry wind that blows over the northern plains in summer.
2. Mango showers occur in the south-west before the monsoon.
3. Kalbaisakhi is a thunderstorm of Punjab and Haryana.
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers) affects West Bengal, Odisha and Assam.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Local storms and winds.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Placing Nor'westers in north-west India.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Placing Nor'westers in north-west India.

questions.text: Which soil is formed by the weathering of basalt, is rich in lime, iron and magnesia but poor in nitrogen and phosphorus, and suits cotton?
questions.explanation: Regur or black soil is formed from the Deccan basalt and holds moisture.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Soil types and crops.
Option A (Alluvial soil) is out: Formed by river deposits.
Option C (Red soil) is out: Formed from crystalline rocks.
Option D (Laterite soil) is out: Formed by leaching in heavy rain.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing alluvial soil because it is fertile.
So the answer is option B: Black soil.
questions.trap: Choosing alluvial soil because it is fertile.
wrongReasons: Formed by leaching in heavy rain

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs of a dam and its river is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Dam is on the Sutlej; the Pong Dam is on the Beas.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Major dams.
Options A, B and D are out: Correctly matched.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing the Sutlej and Beas dams.
So the answer is option C: Bhakra - Beas.
questions.trap: Mixing the Sutlej and Beas dams.

questions.text: Bhavai, a traditional folk theatre form, is associated with which State?
questions.explanation: Bhavai is a Gujarati folk theatre form.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Folk theatre by State.
Option B (Karnataka) is out: Associated with Yakshagana.
Option C (Maharashtra) is out: Associated with Tamasha.
Option D (Uttar Pradesh) is out: Associated with Nautanki.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the better-known State of Yakshagana or Tamasha.
So the answer is option A: Gujarat.
questions.trap: Choosing the better-known State of Yakshagana or Tamasha.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins are the exception where a vein carries oxygenated blood.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Circulatory system.
Option B (Pulmonary artery) is out: Carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
Option C (Vena cava) is out: Brings deoxygenated blood to the right atrium.
Option D (Aorta) is out: Carries oxygenated blood out of the heart.
Common slip to avoid: Assuming veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
So the answer is option A: Pulmonary vein.
questions.trap: Assuming veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
wrongReasons: Carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs
Brings deoxygenated blood to the right atrium
Carries oxygenated blood out of the heart

questions.text: Elena Rybakina won two Grand Slam singles titles in 2026. Which two?
questions.explanation: Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka in both the Australian Open and US Open finals of 2026. Mirra Andreeva won the French Open and Linda Noskova won Wimbledon.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Grand Slams 2026.
Option A (French Open and Wimbledon) is out: Andreeva won the French Open and Noskova won Wimbledon.
Option B (Australian Open and Wimbledon) is out: Wimbledon went to Linda Noskova.
Option C (Wimbledon and US Open) is out: Wimbledon went to Linda Noskova.
Common slip to avoid: Assigning her the Wimbledon title she won in 2022.
So the answer is option D: Australian Open and US Open.
questions.trap: Assigning her the Wimbledon title she won in 2022.
wrongReasons: Andreeva won the French Open and Noskova won Wimbledon

questions.text: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry honoured Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai. Their work concerned which problem?
options: How mirror-image (chiral) molecules come to favour one form
questions.explanation: The 2026 Chemistry prize went to Kagan (France) and Soai (Japan) for work on chirality: why molecules that exist as mirror images end up favouring one form, which matters in drug development.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Nobel Chemistry 2026.
Option A (Metal-organic frameworks that store gases) is out: That was the 2025 Chemistry prize.
Option C (Click chemistry and bioorthogonal reactions) is out: That was the 2022 prize.
Option D (Development of lithium-ion batteries) is out: That was the 2019 prize.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing a topic from an earlier Chemistry prize.
So the answer is option B: How mirror-image (chiral) molecules come to favour one form.
questions.trap: Choosing a topic from an earlier Chemistry prize.

options: Optogenetics, which uses light to switch brain cells on and off

questions.text: In December 2025 the RBI cut the policy repo rate by 25 basis points. To which level was it reduced?
questions.explanation: The MPC reduced the repo rate from 5.50% to 5.25% in December 2025.

Option A (5.50%) is out: This was the rate before the cut.
